中低音薩魯梭風主體採用黃銅或鎳銀製成，提供堅固的金屬外殼與良好的音響傳導。管身內: The body of the baritone sarrusophone is made of brass or nickel silver, giving a sturdy metal shell and good transmission of sound. The bore is mostly brass, which secures a penetrating, resonant timbre. The double reed is made of cane, which gives expression and warmth of tone. The keywork is silver-plated or gold-plated brass for durability. Cork and leather are used for the key pads, which keeps the instrument airtight and gives it a long working life.
中低音薩魯梭風屬薩魯梭風家族的金屬雙簧圓錐管氣鳴樂器，19世紀末至20世紀初主要: The baritone sarrusophone is a metal double-reed, conical-bore aerophone of the sarrusophone family, made from the late nineteenth to the early twentieth century mainly by the inventor, the Paris instrument maker Pierre-Louis Gautrot, and his successor Couesnon & Co., and also by Evette & Schaeffer and by Orsi of Milan. The family was designed to replace the oboe and bassoon in military and marching bands; the metal construction is more durable and easier to hear outdoors. Today only Orsi and the German maker Benedikt Eppelsheim take orders for them.
中低音薩魯梭風是薩魯梭風家族的中低音成員，屬氣鳴樂器，以金屬雙簧圓錐管發聲，調性: The baritone sarrusophone is the baritone member of the sarrusophone family, an aerophone sounded through a metal double reed and a conical tube, pitched in E flat, with the same range as the baritone saxophone and about as tall as a bassoon, the tube making only one turn. It is played with a double reed. The family was designed to replace the oboe and bassoon in military and marching bands; the metal construction is more durable and easier to hear outdoors.
中低音薩魯梭風為氣鳴樂器，屬金屬雙簧、圓錐管構造，音域同中低音薩克斯風。薩魯梭風: The baritone sarrusophone is an aerophone with a metal double reed and a conical bore, with the same range as the baritone saxophone. The sarrusophone family was designed for military and marching bands, to replace the oboe and bassoon; the metal construction is more durable and also easier to hear outdoors. Its actual setting is therefore mainly outdoor forces such as military and marching bands, rather than the music of any particular composer.
中低音薩魯梭風音色渾厚而具有侵略性，兼具金屬樂器的明亮穿透力與雙簧樂器的溫潤感。: The baritone sarrusophone's timbre is full and aggressive, combining the bright penetration of a metal instrument with the warmth of a double reed. Its tone is sharper and more incisive than the bassoon's, with a distinctive metallic quality that makes it easy to pick out in a band. The range is wide: the low register is full and heavy, the middle warm and round, and the high register sharply penetrating. Because of the conical bore the instrument resonates richly and directly and projects strongly, so it can cut through the other parts of a band. Compared with the smoothness of the saxophone the baritone sarrusophone is more angular; compared with the bassoon it is brighter and stronger. This particular sound makes it an indispensable bridging instrument in the wind band.
